summary: tidewatch is a Node CLI that fetches harmonic constituents once and predicts high and low water in the terminal (README.md:3). The 0.2.0 tree supplies next, day, and stations --near (CHANGELOG.md:5, CHANGELOG.md:6, CHANGELOG.md:11). Draft PR #18 tracks the offline constituent cache, ROADMAP.md also lists subordinate-station offsets, and CI runs on Node 20 and 22 (ROADMAP.md:6, ROADMAP.md:8, .github/workflows/ci.yml:8).

goals.text: Correct to within 5 minutes and 3 cm of the published tables for every reference station.
Works offline after the first fetch.
Small: no native dependencies, starts in under 100 ms.

rules.text: Branch from main, name branches feat/<topic> or fix/<topic>, and never push to main directly.
Write conventional commits using feat:, fix:, docs:, and test:.
Every change to the predictor needs a test with numbers from a published table, and the test must name the source.
npm test and npm run lint must pass before a pull request.
No new runtime dependencies without an issue first.
Run npm test before saying a change works, and run npm run lint too.
Heights are metres and times are UTC inside src/, and convert only in src/format.js.
Do not edit src/constituents.json by hand, because it is generated by npm run constituents.
Keep the CLI output stable, because tests compare it byte for byte.
